The defect ledger

Every point where the run CATCHES a defect appends one structured row to the ledger: a containment violation, a unit whose checks never went green, a gate that could not run (exit 126/127 — an infrastructure defect, not a code verdict), a supervisor disclosure (by definition a contract gap), a confession found by the honesty scan, a finding carried to the delivery.

The ledger is one file per month at the store’s root — defects/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl — shared by every space, with each row naming the space it came from. It is not kept inside the space, so deleting a space never deletes the record of what went wrong in it.

Run Tandem: Show Defects to render it as a table.

The rows are find-time facts: what surfaced the defect, and what it cost. Reading them monthly is how the methodology learns. A row that recurs is a process defect, not a code defect — and the fix belongs in the process, not in one more check.
